subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from George Eliot's 1871 novel Middlemarch. Dr. Edward Jenner was a prominent British physician who developed the first smallpox vaccine.

Some years past, a distinguished elderly physician, while attending a medical conference in Edinburgh, noticed a rather shabby young man in ill-fitting clothes, scribbling notes with apparent earnestness but asking what seemed to be elementary questions. The physician felt considerable irritation at this person's presence among serious practitioners; however, finding himself seated beside the fellow at dinner, he engaged in reluctant conversation, only to discover unexpectedly thoughtful observations about medical practice, and was utterly confounded when a colleague later mentioned that the unimpressive stranger was none other than Dr. Edward Jenner.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: It presents an account of a misunderstanding.
choices.B: It portrays the thoughts of a character who feels ashamed about his initial assumptions.
choices.C: It offers a brief explanation of how a person achieved medical recognition.
choices.D: It describes why one character finds another irritating.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The text tells a story of a first impression that turned out to be wrong: a distinguished elderly physician was dismissive of a shabby, questioning young man at a medical conference, and then was shocked to learn that the man was actually a prominent British physician and medical pioneer.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. This is too strong and too narrow. Only at the very end is the physician "utterly confounded" by the fact that the man was Dr. Jenner—he's not "ashamed about his initial assumptions."
